title: Which rules hold for every rectangle and its diagonals?
description: The sides and the eight angles of several rectangles sit in a table, and the patterns that repeat in every row are written as rules. The square is looked at on its own, and each rule is checked against every row.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rule is a pattern that holds in every row of the table, so it is framed from all the rows and checked against all of them. Watch for students who frame a rule from one row, such as that a diagonal always cuts a corner in half.

video_script.why: A learner reads a table of measurements of several rectangles and frames the rules that hold in every row, as the book's solved examples measure and compare.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle PQRS with its sides and its eight angles a to h, taken for several rectangles
video_script.anchor: the book's rectangle PQRS with both diagonals and the eight angles named
video_script.payoff_line: In every rectangle opposite sides are equal, and the diagonals are equal.

final_answer.value: opposite sides equal; all angles 90 degrees; diagonals equal; the two angles at a corner add up to 90 degrees; in a square they are 45 degrees and 45 degrees
final_answer.spoken: opposite sides are equal, the diagonals are equal, and the two angles at a corner add up to ninety degrees

maths_rules: opposite sides of a rectangle are equal and every angle is 90 degrees
the two diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length
the two angles a diagonal makes at a corner add up to 90 degrees
the eight angles fall into two groups of four equal angles
in a square the two angles at a corner are 45 degrees and 45 degrees, because 45 + 45 = 90
video_script.design: A small table of rectangles stays on the board. Each rule is lit up in every row before it is written, and the square row is marked apart.
